To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the geometries of nucleobases in the T(0) and T(1) states are optimized using the analytic gradients in combined second-order Møller-Plessen perturbation theory and the conductor-like polarizable continuum model.

in the T( 1) state the hydrogen bonds in adenine-thymidine and adenine- uracil pairs are weakened by about 1 kcal/mol as compare to those in S(0) states, but the hydrogen bond in the guanine-cytidine pair is not weakened.
the hydrogen bonds in T(1) nucleobase pairs are weaker than those in S(0) nucleobase pair, and that the T(1)-T(1) energy gap is larger for the gas phase than for the aqueous solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an analytic energy gradient method in combined second order many-body perturbation theory and continuum solvation model calculations, and with the applications of the new methods to study the geometries of three DNA base pairs in the ground and first excited states in both the gas and the aqueous phase.
the study of the electronic excited state of nucleobase pairs in the gas phase as well as in the aqueous solution.

the application of combined second order Moller-Plesset perturbational theory and conductorlike solvation model in the calculation of the ground state and the excited T-1 states of the nucleobase pairs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the gas phase, the T(1)/S(0) excitation energy of the nucleobase pair increases as the hydrogen bonds are weakened, while in aqueous solution the T(1)-S(0) energy difference decreases as the hydrogen bonds weaken.
the hydrogen bonds in both the S(0)-state and T(1)-state nucleobase pairs in aqueous solution are stronger than those in the gas phase.
, in aqueous solution phase, both the S(0)-S(1) and S(0)-T(1) energy gaps decrease with the increasing solvent dielectric constant, while the S(0)/T(1) geometry change is not significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combined second order MØller-Plesset theory and the conductorlike polarizable continuous model are a very useful and accurate method for studying the geometries of excited states of nucleobase pairs in the aqueous solution.

the combined second order MØller-Plesset and conductorlike polarisable continuum model calculations can give accurate geometries of the excited states of the nucleobase pairs in both the gas and aqueous solution phases.

, for the first time, the geometries for both the ground state and the excited state of nucleobase pairs have been optimized in both the gas and aqueous solution phases, which is of fundamental importance to the understanding of the photochemical reaction mechanism in nucleobase pairs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometry optimization using the conductorlike polarizable continuous model is a useful tool for the study of the excited state of nucleobases and nucleobase pairs.
the S(0)-T(1) energy gaps in the gas phase are 0.5-1.0 kcal/mol smaller than the corresponding energy gaps in the aqueous solution phases.
the combined second order Moller-Plesset perturbative method and conductorlike polarized continuum model can be a useful tool for investigating excited state structures in aqueous solution.
